target.title: RFC 0019: Managed configuration
target.body:
## Why this RFC exists

Lobster needs to combine Scout-wide defaults, tenant-specific URLs/private-network facts, and operator-local OpenClaw settings.

Today Lobster does that outside OpenClaw by baking overlays into one effective config and maintaining overlay application, validation alignment, and stale-value cleanup. OpenClaw sees only the result, so it cannot reject a later overlay that conflicts with or weakens an earlier boundary.

We want one official OpenClaw-supported, opt-in seam instead of host-specific overlay machinery.

## Proposed V1

RFC 0019 now matches the simplified implementation:

- repeat `--config-layer <id=path>` in declared order
- treat every source as an ordinary sparse OpenClaw JSON5 config document
- resolve includes/env and run normal schema/plugin validation
- compose objects recursively
- let the earliest declaration own an exact path
- allow later `tools.allow` and `tools.deny` values only when they provably tighten policy
- publish one startup-only, read-only runtime snapshot
- keep layer names generic; core has no host, tenant, operator, or two-stage roles
- keep ordinary no-flag config behavior unchanged

The prior RFC draft described writable layers, provenance APIs, live reload, rollback, and a larger PR stack. Those are now explicit future work, not part of V1.

## Lobster example

Lobster materializes three normal files.

`scout-global.json5` owns fleet security defaults:

```json5
{
  gateway: {
    mode: "local",
    auth: { mode: "trusted-proxy" },
  },
  tools: { deny: ["exec"] },
}
```

`tenant-network.json5` adds tenant-specific connectivity:

```json5
{
  gateway: {
    bind: "tailnet",
    controlUi: {
      allowedOrigins: ["https://openclaw.acme.internal"],
    },
  },
  tools: { deny: ["exec", "web"] },
}
```

`operator.json5` adds local customization on unrelated paths:

```json5
{
  gateway: { controlUi: { enabled: true } },
  logging: { level: "info" },
}
```

Startup is explicit:

```bash
openclaw gateway run \
  --config-layer scout=./scout-global.json5 \
  --config-layer tenant=./tenant-network.json5 \
  --config-layer operator=./operator.json5
```

If the operator file tries to replace the tenant origin or remove `web` from the inherited deny policy, startup is rejected. The RFC includes the complete effective config and architecture/recursive-fold diagrams.

## Evidence

- Broad exploratory fork prototype: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/33
- Simplified upstream implementation draft: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107026
- Lobster fork adapter materializes the three documents and passes repeated flags
- 61 focused OpenClaw tests pass
- Final OpenClaw Codex review: no actionable correctness regression
- RFC Codex review: no actionable correctness issue

The broad prototype demonstrated the lifecycle constraints; the smaller upstream draft is the proposed implementation.

## Delivery plan

1. Land the complete OpenClaw V1 after green upstream CI and a recorded foreground lifecycle proof.
2. After an OpenClaw release contains it, adopt that release in Lobster and delete the baked overlay writer, stale-value cleanup, and exact generated-blob tests.

## Scope

This PR changes only `rfcs/0019-managed-configuration.md`. It remains a draft while the linked OpenClaw implementation is reviewed.
